contract: construct() -> nonempty list of distinct integers in [0, 2**N). Each integer encodes one N-bit binary codeword, including leading zeros. Every pair must have Hamming distance at least MINIMUM_DISTANCE. Linear and nonlinear codes are allowed. Score: number of codewords, maximized.
notes: Independent exact pairwise Hamming-distance verifier for A_2(18,6). The seed is a 32-word Reed-Muller subconstruction. Tests reconstruct the 512-word extended quadratic-residue reference using g(x)=x^8+x^5+x^4+x^3+1 and verify all 130,816 pairs. The 2012 source establishes an upper bound of 673, and Brouwer's table lists 512..673 when inspected on 2026-09-20; the evaluator does not assume that bound or claim global optimality. This task searches constructions, not the paper's semidefinite upper-bound program.
protocol_description: Reimplemented in this repository and cross-checked against the paper's published constructions/values.
name: Binary error-correcting codes of length 18 and distance 6
description: Construct the largest possible collection of 18-bit words with pairwise Hamming distance at least 6, the extremal quantity A_2(18,6). Both linear and nonlinear codes are allowed. Every pair is checked exactly using integer XOR and population count. The initial Reed-Muller construction has 32 words; a 512-word extended quadratic-residue construction is independently verified as a reference.
benchmark: Binary error-correcting codes of length 18 and distance 6
paper_metric: Local protocol; see candidate contract and source adaptation notes

sources.locator: Gijswijt, Mittelmann and Schrijver, Semidefinite code bounds based on quadruple distances (2012): definition of A(n,d), and the upper bound A(18,6) <= 673.
Brouwer's table of general binary codes, row n=18 and column d=6, lists 512..673; inspected 2026-09-20. Used as dated research context, not as an evaluator-enforced bound.

ETSI TS 102 361-1 V2.3.1, Annex B.3.2, printed page 132, equation (B.2): primitive (17,9,5) quadratic-residue generator g(x)=x^8+x^5+x^4+x^3+1. Tests use all nine message bits and append even parity to obtain a verified (18,512,6) reference, rather than the standard's shortened (16,7,6) code.

limitations: The source paper derives upper bounds with semidefinite programming. This task recreates its finite code-construction question and objective, not its SDP algorithm or experiments.

The reference is reconstructed from a published quadratic-residue generator and verified over every pair; the encoder is a local implementation and is extended to 18 bits rather than shortened as in the ETSI example.

The 512..673 interval is dated source context, not a claim of an optimum or a permanently current record. The evaluator assumes only the elementary Hamming bound, derived directly from disjoint Hamming balls.
Improving the 32-word seed or reaching 512 words does not settle the open extremal problem. Any proposed new record needs separate comparison with current constructions and upper bounds.
